Consent




To participate in the study, please read the following statements:





- I confirm that I have read the participant information sheet for this study. I was given the opportunity to ask questions, and they have been answered to my satisfaction. I was given sufficient time to decide whether I want to participate.



- I confirm that my participation is voluntary and that I am allowed to withdraw from the study at any time, without providing a reason.



- I consent to my data being collected and processed, and that the data will only be used for this research project. Additionally, the results of the research will only be published anonymously.



- I understand that my data can be viewed by other researchers to check whether the research has been conducted according to the rules.



- I understand that students under the supervision of the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam are involved in this study as part of their bachelor thesis, and that they have access to my personal data after signing a privacy statement. I consent to these students accessing my personal data for research purposes only.



- I understand that my data will be kept confidential, and that, if sharing data with third parties is needed, only de-identified data will be shared.



- I understand that my data will be saved for 10 years after participation, and therefore I give consent.



- I would like to voluntarily participate in this research project.

Debriefing:
Participant Debriefing Sheet
Dear Participant,

Thank you for taking the time to participate in this project!



In this survey, we were interested in collecting personality data, various background variables and how they may be related to the selection of situations. Specifically, the HEXACO personality questionnaire is a self-reported measure that allows us to create a profile of a person based on six different traits: Honesty-Humility, Emotionality, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness and Openness to Experience. This will allow us to understand how people differ in terms of behavioral and emotional tendencies. Other data collected are: educational background, job experiences and other job-related questions to help us understand the differences in participants’ work and life experiences.

For this study, you read six pairs of vignettes that portrayed companies that were manipulated to reflect differences in situational components related to personality traits. These components that are related to personality are called situational affordances, and they represent the presence, or absence, of situational components that make it more likely for people to express behavior related to the aligned personality trait. For example, the situational cues that could be present at a party can make it more likely for people to behave more socially. The situational affordances are six, each one related to the personality traits. The situational cues were manipulated to reflect a higher (or lower) likelihood of the expression of a behavior related to a personality trait. By manipulating the situational cues offered by each company, we were able to see if personality traits are related to your preferences and selection of situations.

Additionally, you rated each vignette on a modified version of the Domain-Specific-Situational-Affordances (DSSA) scale, which is a scale that allows for the rating of the six situational affordances. These ratings indicate how you perceived the presence, and the strength, of each of the six situational affordances, regardless of which one was manipulated. The ratings will be used to investigate if personality traits are related to the perception of these situational cues, and to establish if a person's score on a personality trait can predict their perception of the aligned situational affordance. Ultimately, with this study, we will have a better understanding of how personality is related to the selection of situations, the perception of situational cues and if there are any background variables that may play a role.



We thank you again for contributing to the study! If you have follow-up questions, are interested in learning more about the study and its outcome, or if you have any other possible questions, comments, or complaints, please use the contact information provided below to contact the researcher.



Contact information:

Principal Investigator: Lorenzo Cupri (l.cupri@vu.nl)

Promotor: Reinout de Vries (re.de.vries@vu.nl)

Supervisor: Ard Barends (a.j.barends@law.leidenuniv.nl)
